title: Passengers, operations and cargo by airport, AENA network (2025, final)
publisher: Aena; airport positions from OurAirports
license: AENA statistics: reproduction subject to Aena's legal notice; OurAirports: public domain
description: Passengers (arrivals plus departures), aircraft operations and cargo of the 47 airports and heliports of the AENA network in 2025. Each is placed with OurAirports, matched by the words of its name.

title: Atlas Digital de las Áreas Urbanas: large urban areas and their municipalities (2025)
publisher: Ministerio de Vivienda y Agenda Urbana (Atlas Digital de las Áreas Urbanas de España)
license: Public-sector information, reuse permitted citing the source (Ley 37/2007)
description: The 86 large urban areas (Grandes Áreas Urbanas: over 50,000 residents) and the municipalities each one is made of, as defined by the ministry. They are the map's cities, like the US metro areas: a city's population, jobs and footprint add up its member municipalities.
used_for: Cities (urban areas) and their member municipalities

title: Blue Flag beaches 2026-2027 (Bandera Azul, ADEAC)
publisher: ADEAC (Asociación de Educación Ambiental y del Consumidor), Blue Flag programme
license: © ADEAC; the list of awarded beaches is cited as published
description: Every Spanish beach awarded the Blue Flag for 2026-2027, by municipality, as ADEAC lists them in its PDF (read into pipeline/sources/es/data/bandera_azul_2026.csv; the count per community matches ADEAC's).

title: Protected food and drink names: their areas (MAPA) and the EU register (eAmbrosia)
publisher: Ministerio de Agricultura, Pesca y Alimentación; European Commission (eAmbrosia)
license: MAPA: CC BY 4.0; eAmbrosia: European Commission reuse notice (CC BY 4.0)
description: The geographical area of each Spanish protected designation of origin (DOP), protected geographical indication (IGP), quality wine and vino de pago, as the Ministry maps them (last revised in 2017, so names registered since then have no area yet), and the count of names Spain has in the EU register.

title: CORINE Land Cover 2018 (via the IDEE land-cover WMS)
publisher: Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (EEA); served by the Instituto Geográfico Nacional (IDEE)
license: CC BY 4.0 (scne.es) for the IDEE service; CORINE Land Cover is Copernicus data under its free, full and open data policy
description: Land cover in 44 CORINE classes for Spain, read from the IDEE INSPIRE land-cover map (EPSG:3035, 500 m pixels, the size of CORINE's 25 ha minimum mapping unit) by the exact colours of the standard CLC legend. Each class is cross-walked to an NLCD class (built-up 111/112/12x → developed, arable and permanent crops → cultivated, 231 pastures and 244 dehesas → pasture, 31x forests, 321 grassland, 32x and 333 scrub, 33x bare → barren, 4xx wetlands, 5xx water) so the map uses one set of cover rules for every country.

title: ETOPO1 global relief model (Spain, full resolution)
publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (via ERDDAP)
license: Public domain (U.S. Government work)
description: Land elevation and sea depth every 1 arc-minute (~1.85 km), about 25 samples per 10 km hex. Each hex's relief (flat, hills, mountains, peaks) comes from the mean and roughness of the land samples inside it.

title: Household income distribution atlas (ADRH): mean and median income indicators, table 30824
publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE)
license: CC BY 4.0 (INE legal notice): commercial and non-commercial reuse, citing the source as "Elaboración propia con datos del INE"; INE does not endorse this map
description: Net income from the tax records of the Agencia Tributaria and the regional treasuries, matched to the Padrón, for every municipality (and its census districts and sections, which are not used here). The map uses the mean net income per person of each municipality, the latest year INE publishes. Small municipalities can be missing (statistical confidentiality); they stay without data.
vintage: INE Atlas de Distribución de Renta de los Hogares, 2024

title: Annual Population Census: employed residents by CNAE division, Spain and main cities (tables 69960 and 69980)
publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE)
license: CC BY 4.0 (INE legal notice): commercial and non-commercial reuse, citing the source as "Elaboración propia con datos del INE"; INE does not endorse this map
description: Employed people aged 16 and over by the two-digit CNAE-2009 division of their job (88 divisions), for Spain and its provinces (table 69960) and for the provincial capitals and main cities (151 municipalities, table 69980), counted where they live. Used for districts: each city's industry specialisation against the national share.
vintage: INE Censo anual de población (Ocupación y actividad), 1 January 2024

title: Annual Population Census: employed residents by CNAE section (tables 69962 and 69992)
publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE)
license: CC BY 4.0 (INE legal notice): commercial and non-commercial reuse, citing the source as "Elaboración propia con datos del INE"; INE does not endorse this map
description: Employed people aged 16 and over by the CNAE-2009 section (A…U) of their job, counted where they live (like the US map's ACS), from the Annual Population Census (Ocupación y actividad): Spain and the provinces (table 69962) and every municipality of 500 residents or more (table 69992). The sections are mapped to the map's industries; 'No consta' (not stated) counts in the total only.
used_for: Food, Production, Science and Culture yields
vintage: INE Censo anual de población (Ocupación y actividad), 1 January 2024

title: Official population figures by municipality (Padrón municipal revision), table 29005
publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE)
license: CC BY 4.0 (INE legal notice): commercial and non-commercial reuse, citing the source as "Elaboración propia con datos del INE"; INE does not endorse this map
description: Residents of every municipality on 1 January of each year since 1996, from the yearly revision of the municipal registers (Padrón). Provinces and Spain are the sums of their municipalities.

title: GDP at market prices by province, current prices (Contabilidad Regional de España), table 80109
publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE)
license: CC BY 4.0 (INE legal notice): commercial and non-commercial reuse, citing the source as "Elaboración propia con datos del INE"; INE does not endorse this map
description: Gross domestic product at market prices in current euros for Spain, its autonomous communities and provinces (thousands of euros in the table). The single-province communities (Madrid, Asturias, Cantabria, Murcia, Navarra, La Rioja, the Balearic Islands, Ceuta and Melilla) appear only as communities and are used as their province. Spain's total also counts the extra-regional territory (embassies, bases abroad), which no province has.
used_for: Gold yield (GDP) of provinces and Spain

title: Official regional languages by municipality (Navarre's language zones, Valencian-speaking area)
publisher: Gobierno de Navarra (IDENA); Agencia Estatal Boletín Oficial del Estado
license: IDENA: CC BY 4.0; BOE: legal texts, free reuse
description: The language zones of Navarre (Ley Foral 18/1986, as amended in 2017) and the municipalities where Castilian predominates in the Valencian Community (Llei 4/1983, art. 36); with the regions where a language is co-official everywhere, they give each municipality its official languages.

title: Natural Earth 1:10m (countries, lakes, rivers) around Spain
publisher: Natural Earth
license: Public domain
description: Neighbouring countries (Portugal, France, Andorra, Gibraltar, Morocco; shown fogged), lakes and reservoirs, and rivers. At 1:10m, so the 10 km hexes get the Ebro's, Tajo's and Guadalquivir's tributaries too. Files are pinned to the natural-earth-vector release v5.1.2.

title: Natural Earth 1:10m roads and railroads around Spain
publisher: Natural Earth
license: Public domain
description: Motorways (autovías and autopistas), main roads and railroads as 1:10m line work. Shown as map art (roads and rail between hex centres), not as statistics: Natural Earth carries no traffic or owner data and holds only the main lines. Files are pinned to the natural-earth-vector release v5.1.2.
used_for: Motorways and main roads on the map

title: National Park boundaries (Red de Parques Nacionales)
publisher: Organismo Autónomo Parques Nacionales (OAPN), Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica
license: Public-sector information, reuse permitted citing the source (Ley 37/2007); the service declares no access constraints or fees
description: The boundaries of Spain's 16 National Parks as declared by law, with their declaration date and official area, from the OAPN's map server, and their 2025 visitors from the OAPN's yearly report (a PDF, transcribed in pipeline/sources/es/data). The special protection area around the Sierra de Guadarrama is not a National Park and is left out.
vintage: OAPN, Red de Parques Nacionales; visitors 2025

title: Peoples of ancient Iberia (Pleiades)
publisher: Pleiades (Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, NYU, and contributors)
license: CC BY 3.0
description: Every place Pleiades types as a people with a located point in and around the Iberian Peninsula (Vaccaei, Vascones, Cantabri, Ilergetes, the many peoples of Gallaecia…), plus the regions it names after peoples it has no point for (Turdetania, Bastetania, Contestania, Edetania, Carpetania, Celtiberia, Cessetania, Laeetania). A '?' marks an uncertain location, as in Pleiades.

title: Power plants in Spain (powerplantmatching; OpenStreetMap for the Canary Islands)
publisher: PyPSA powerplantmatching (KIT and contributors); OpenStreetMap contributors
license: powerplantmatching data: CC BY 4.0; OpenStreetMap: ODbL 1.0
description: Every power plant powerplantmatching lists in Spain (a merge of ENTSO-E, GEM, OPSD, JRC and other registers), with its fuel, capacity, location and commissioning and retirement years, pinned to commit 2889ad9d1. It has no plant on the Canary Islands, so those come from OpenStreetMap's power=plant objects that state their capacity.

title: Freight traffic by Port Authority (2025) and port service areas
publisher: Puertos del Estado
license: Service areas: CC BY 4.0 (datos.gob.es); traffic statistics: Puertos del Estado's legal notice
description: Total freight traffic in tonnes of each of the 28 Port Authorities in 2025 (December cumulative), placed at the land service area of their largest port.

title: SIANE municipal boundaries and capitals, 1:3 million (Atlas Nacional de España)
publisher: Instituto Geográfico Nacional (IGN), republished by rOpenSpain/mapSpain
license: CC BY 4.0: Atlas Nacional de España (ANE), ign.es
description: Outlines of Spain's municipalities in force (INE code) and the position of each municipality's capital. Each hex belongs to the municipality and province most of its seven sample points fall in; provinces are the union of their municipalities and of the territories several municipalities share (condominios). Cities sit at their municipal capital.

title: University students by centre and the municipality of each centre (SIIU, 2024-2025)
publisher: Sistema Integrado de Información Universitaria, Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovación y Universidades
license: Reuse permitted, commercial or not, citing the Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovación y Universidades
description: Students enrolled in degree, master's and doctoral programmes in 2024-2025 at every centre of every Spanish university, with the municipality of each centre and whether the university teaches on site.

title: Wikidata: World Heritage sites, cathedrals, museums and Bienes de Interés Cultural in Spain
publisher: Wikidata (Wikimedia Foundation and volunteer editors)
license: CC0 1.0 (public domain dedication)
description: Items in Spain designated World Heritage (grouped by their UNESCO site number), cathedrals and co-cathedrals, museums, and Bienes de Interés Cultural, with their coordinates, from Wikidata's SPARQL service. Volunteer-edited: coverage is close to, but not exactly, the official registers.
